meta.promptText: Which vitamin C serum should I buy for dark spots and dull skin in India?

response.text:
For **dark spots + dull skin**, I’d start with a **10% vitamin C serum** rather than jumping straight to 15–20%. Stable vitamin-C derivatives are generally easier to tolerate, and consistency matters more than using the highest percentage. [phdbeauty.com](https://phdbeauty.com/blogs/general-advice/best-vitamin-c-serum-india-2026?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[www.pingmedoc.com](https://www.pingmedoc.com/pharmacy/buying-guides/best-vitamin-c-serum?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

### My picks in India

**1. Best overall: Minimalist 10% Vitamin C**  
### [Minimalist Face Serum]()
*₹629*

A good choice if you're new to vitamin C or want something relatively gentle. It uses **10% ethyl ascorbic acid**, a stable derivative, and is particularly sensible if pigmentation is accompanied by easily irritated skin. [www.mrpuku.com](https://www.mrpuku.com/2026/02/Vitamin-C-Serum.html?m=1&utm_source=chatgpt.com)

**2. If your skin already tolerates actives: Plum 15% Vitamin C**  
### [Plum 15% Vitamin C Face Serum Mandarin]()
*₹457*

A stronger option for someone who has already used vitamin C/acids without irritation. Current Indian product roundups specifically include it among options for dullness and pigmentation. [phdbeauty.com](https://phdbeauty.com/blogs/general-advice/best-vitamin-c-serum-india-2026?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[www.pingmedoc.com](https://www.pingmedoc.com/pharmacy/buying-guides/best-vitamin-c-serum?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

**3. Budget-friendly alternative: Fixderma 17% Vitamin C**  
### [Fixderma 17% Vitamin C Face Serum]()
*₹380*

I'd choose this only if your skin is fairly tolerant—the higher percentage isn't automatically better and can increase irritation.

### How I'd use it

**Morning:** cleanser → vitamin C serum → moisturizer → **SPF 50+ sunscreen**.

The sunscreen is crucial: UV exposure can keep dark spots coming back, so vitamin C without consistent sunscreen will give you much less benefit. Improvement in pigmentation generally takes **several weeks to a few months**, rather than days. [www.whowhatwear.com](https://www.whowhatwear.com/beauty/skin/best-products-for-hyperpigmentation?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

**My simple recommendation:** if you haven't used vitamin C before, **buy Minimalist 10%**. If you've already used vitamin C and your skin is comfortable with actives, **Plum 15%** is the more aggressive choice.

If you tell me your **skin type (oily/dry/combination/sensitive), age, and budget (₹500/₹1,000/₹2,000+)**, I can narrow it down to **one exact serum** for you.

sources.snippet:
This article from Who What Wear UK provides a comprehensive guide to the best skincare products for treating hyperpigmentation, featuring insights from dermatologists and skin experts. Hyperpigmentation, a common skin concern caused by excess melanin, can result from sun exposure, hormonal changes (such as pregnancy-related melasma), inflammation, or acne scarring. The guide emphasizes that the cause of pigmentation determines the best treatment and underlines the importance of daily SPF use as the most critical step in both prevention and treatment.

Recommended ingredients include vitamin C, niacinamide, azelaic acid, tranexamic acid, and retinoids, which can be found in both over-the-counter and prescription products. Experts caution that results typically take 6 to 12 weeks, or even months, and consistency in skincare is essential.

The article highlights 13 carefully selected products, spanning cleansers, serums, moisturizers, and SPFs. Notable mentions include La Roche-Posay Mela B3 Cleanser, Eucerin Pigment Control SPF50+, The Ordinary Azelaic Acid 10%, and Murad Rapid Dark Spot Correcting Serum. Each product is chosen based on expert input, performance, ingredient quality, and user reviews, providing practical options for anyone tackling dark spots and uneven skin tone.
